title: Behind Ibrahim's station
hook: two units of prayer behind the station of Ibrahim (2:125)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the black stone, and your line: a salute to the corner. What small gesture did you make from where you stood? Day one thousand one hundred twenty-seven.

The seventh circuit ends at the corner of the stone. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ has gone around the House, and the crowd is still turning. Jabir ibn Abdullah, who told the story of that pilgrimage, says what came next, in a report kept in Sahih Muslim. The Prophet stepped out of the circle and walked a short way to a spot near the Ka'ba. As he went, he recited a line from the Qur'an. Then he stood, with that spot between him and the House, and prayed. Today, the place he stopped.
screen: `THE SEVENTH CIRCUIT ENDS.` → `HE STEPS OUT OF THE CIRCLE.` → `HE STANDS, AND PRAYS.`

segments.voice: First, the verse he recited. It's in surah two, and in Pickthall's translation it reads: "Take as your place of worship the place where Abraham stood (to pray)." The Arabic name is maqam Ibrahim, the station of Ibrahim. Tradition says it's a stone Ibrahim stood on while he and his son built the House; today it sits in a small enclosure near the Ka'ba. Second, what the Prophet did there. Jabir says he placed the station between himself and the House and prayed two units of prayer, two rak'ahs. Jabir also reports what he recited in them: two short surahs, the one that begins Say: He is Allah, One, and the one that begins Say: O disbelievers. Abdullah ibn Umar, in Sahih al-Bukhari, gives the same order: the circuits, then two rak'ahs behind the station, then on to the next rite. Third, the posture of the place. After all the moving, the crowd, the circling, the reaching for the stone, the pilgrim stops and stands where Ibrahim is said to have stood, and prays toward the same House. The circle turns into a line, one person facing one direction. Fourth, look back at the week, because this is where it lands. The boundary, where the pilgrim stepped in. The two white cloths. The restraint the cloth stands for. Here I am, said out loud for miles. Seven circuits around the center. A kiss, a touch, or a raised hand at the corner. And now two quiet rak'ahs at the place of the man who, in the Qur'an, built the House and called the people to it. Each piece this week has been one step. This one is the pause between them.
screen: `TAKE AS YOUR PLACE OF WORSHIP.` · `TWO RAK'AHS BEHIND THE STATION.` · `THE CIRCLE TURNS INTO A LINE.` · `A WEEK OF STEPS, THEN A PAUSE.`

segments.voice: The practice: pray two units, or stand for two. If you're Muslim and pray, you can pray two rak'ahs now, and if you know them, recite the two short surahs the Prophet chose. If you don't pray, stand still for a minute and face one direction, any direction, on purpose. Feet steady. Hands at rest. Let the week's movement settle into one place. Then sit, and breathe. The bell holds the time.
Behind Ibrahim's station. The spot near the Ka'ba where pilgrims pray two rak'ahs after tawaf, following the verse and the Prophet's example. Today's word.
Your line: where ibrahim stood. Today, after something busy ends, stop for one minute before starting the next thing. Day one thousand one hundred twenty-seven.

howItsDone: After completing tawaf, pilgrims pray two rak'ahs behind the station of Ibrahim if there is room, or elsewhere in the mosque when it is crowded, often reciting al-Kafirun and al-Ikhlas.

notes: Pickthall 2:125 quoted from memory, including the parenthesis: confirm exact wording.
Sahih Muslim 1218 (Jabir: placed the station between himself and the House, prayed two rak'ahs reciting al-Ikhlas and al-Kafirun): confirm number and the order of the surahs.
Bukhari 395 (Ibn Umar: seven circuits, two rak'ahs behind the station, then Safa and Marwa): confirm number (also 1627).
'Tradition says it's a stone Ibrahim stood on while he and his son built the House': attributed to tradition; 2:127 (Ibrahim and Ismail raising the foundations) cited for the building. Confirm.
'Today it sits in a small enclosure near the Ka'ba': general description; confirm.
Week-end look-back covers days 1121–1127 (miqat to the station).
howItsDone: praying elsewhere in the mosque when crowded is a standard ruling; confirm.
